title: Spin - resolved momentum distributions and vortex evolution in multiphoton pair production within a modified two-level model
authors: Qi-Rong Wang, Hong-Hao Fan, Musajan Kadir, Ying Wu, Bai-Song Xie
abstract: We investigate spin-resolved momentum distributions and phase vortices in multiphoton electron-positron pair production within a modified two-level model. This model retains the diagonal spinor inner-product terms neglected in the adiabatic approximation, thereby inducing spin-resolved transverse asymmetries in the momentum distribution. For a circularly polarized pulse, the handedness determines the winding direction of the quantized vortices, whereas for a linearly polarized pulse, the phase distribution exhibits nodal lines rather than quantized vortices. For two time-delayed circularly polarized pulses, the time delay introduces a relative phase that governs the multiphoton interference, which in turn drives the vortex evolution in each spin configuration. These results demonstrate that pulse polarization and time delay enable coherent control over vortex topology in pair production.
summary: This theoretical work examines how the polarization and time delay of intense laser pulses control the topological properties, specifically quantized vortices, generated during multiphoton pair production. By using a modified two-level model, the authors show that these external parameters enable coherent control over the angular momentum structure of the created electron-positron pairs.
main_problem: The paper investigates the spin-resolved momentum distributions and the formation and evolution of phase vortices during multiphoton electron-positron pair production.
main_result: The polarization state (circular vs. linear) and the time delay between two pulses allow for coherent control over the topological structure (vortex topology) of the pair production process.
method: The analysis uses a modified two-level model (mTLM) derived from the Dirac equation in the presence of a strong, time-dependent external electromagnetic field.
model_or_system: The system is pair production in a strong external electric field, modeled by the Dirac equation solved via a two-level approximation. The model incorporates spinor inner-product terms neglected in simpler adiabatic treatments.
key_observables: Spin-resolved momentum distributions ($f_{s,s'}(\mathbf{p})$), topological charge ($l_{s,s'}$), and the phase distribution ($\phi_{s,s'}$).
important_parameters: Pulse polarization (LCP, RCP, LP), time delay ($T$), and the strength of the external field.
main_assumptions: The external field is assumed to be spatially homogeneous, and the analysis often sets $p_z=0$ for primary results.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the electric fields for various polarizations (LCP, RCP, LP) and show the resulting spin-resolved momentum and phase distributions for different pulse configurations and time delays.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the general Dirac equation formalism to derive the two-level evolution equations (mTLM). It then analyzes specific polarization cases (single pulse, two pulses) to demonstrate how polarization and time delay control the resulting topological features.
why_interesting: The connection between external field geometry (polarization/time delay) and the topological structure (vortices) of quantum particle creation is highly relevant to non-perturbative quantum optics and strong-field physics.
